transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Louise Schiavone.
President Trump is wrapping up the last weekend before midterm elections with two rallies,
one in Iowa, one in Kansas.
Every seat in the House of Representatives is on the ballot this year, while Republicans
hold a small majority, a power shift looms with the flip of just a few seats when polls
close on November 3rd.
President Trump drove the message home at his rally in Dubuque, Iowa.
People would say, "Oh, it's only a couple of votes."
Those couple of votes, because of the power that they have in terms of the majority, those
couple of votes will dominate politics.
In Michigan, meanwhile, Hailey Stevens, who had competed against Abdul El-Sayed for the
Democratic Party Senate nomination, has now endorsed the Republican Mike Rogers.
States are reporting a surge of early voting in a field that so far seems to be favoring
Democrats.
NPR's Stefan Bassaha reports that the cost of living is at the top of many voters' minds.
Republicans were betting economic issues would be on their side after they passed massive
tax cuts last year.
This year, tax refunds have been about 12 percent larger than last.
But registered Republican Owen Smith in Des Moines, Iowa, says he can't remember if his
tax refund was bigger.
I do my taxes like everyone else one time a year.
So any impact that that may have had on my thoughts at the time of voting is way in the
rear view compared to the gas prices that I'm seeing every single day.
Smith ended up splitting his ticket locally, but voted for Democrats nationally due to
the U.S. war against Iran.
Steven Bassaha, NPR News.
Connecticut's junior U.S. Senator Chris Murphy has been hospitalized following a stroke yesterday.
That's according to a statement from his office.
From Connecticut public radio, Chris Polanski has more.
Shortly after news of Murphy's hospitalization broke, Connecticut's Democratic Governor Ned
Lamont spoke to reporters at a Get Out the Vote rally.
He's been hit by a sudden shock.
He's going to be fine.
And I look forward to walking the state of Connecticut with him very soon.
He's a fighter.
He'll be back.
He'll be back soon.
The 53-year-old Murphy is not on Tuesday's ballot, but has been active on the campaign
trail with fellow Democrats.
His office says he's awake and alert, and they're optimistic for a full recovery.
For NPR News, I'm Chris Polanski in Hartford, Connecticut.
In Arizona, floodwaters rose rapidly today, and in Sedona, officials ordered residents
to evacuate immediately.
Rain fell nearly nonstop and flagstaffed flooding streets and overwhelming drains.
In Colorado, the San Juan River is expected to crest at more than 20 feet tonight.
It's part of a severe weather system of heavy rain resulting in flash flooding in parts
of the southwest.
In Tucson, Arizona, the National Weather Service reported that some locations were on track
to get two or three months of rain in a couple of days.
This is NPR.
Today is the first day of open enrollment for the Affordable Care Act marketplaces, including
healthcare.gov.
As NPR's Selena Simmons-Duffin reports, the markets lost millions of enrollees last
year.
The marketplaces are designed for people who don't qualify for a public program, like
Medicare or Medicaid, and who don't get health insurance through their jobs.
Enrollment on healthcare.gov, which is run by the federal government and all of the state-run
marketplaces, hit a record of 24 million in 2025.
This year, that number dropped by nearly 3 million.
The Trump administration claims the decline in enrollment is a result of weeding out people
who were ineligible or "fantom enrollees."
Health experts say that it's more likely due to higher costs.
Republicans in Congress declined to extend extra money that kept premiums more affordable.
Open enrollment runs until at least January 15th.
The exact deadline varies by state.
Selena Simmons-Duffin, NPR News.
At the box office this weekend, a documentary film was the big draw with Halloween movie
attendance low, the Elizabeth Holmes documentary "You Can See Everything" led ticket sales.
The film has grossed $64 million so far.
I'm Louise Schiavone, NPR News, Washington.

topics.text: President Trump holds final pre-midterm rallies in Dubuque, Iowa and Kansas
Hailey Stevens endorses Republican Mike Rogers in Michigan Senate race
Early voting surges nationally, with a field that so far seems to favor Democrats
Iowa voter Owen Smith says gas prices outweigh smaller tax refunds in voting decisions
Connecticut Senator Chris Murphy hospitalized after stroke; office says he is alert
Flash flooding forces evacuations in Sedona, Arizona, and swamps Flagstaff and Tucson
San Juan River in Colorado expected to crest above 20 feet amid southwest flooding
ACA marketplace open enrollment begins; enrollment falls nearly 3 million from last year
Elizabeth Holmes documentary 'You Can See Everything' leads weekend box office with $64 million
